summary.headline: Ashoka Buildcon Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA fell 7% to INR168 crores; FY27 guidance calls for 20% revenue growth and 9.5-10.5% margin.
summary.overview: Standalone total income fell 10% YoY to INR1,819 crores in Q4 FY26, with EBITDA of INR168 crores (9.2% margin, up 20 bps) and PAT of INR49 crores versus INR60 crores a year earlier. For FY26, standalone total income declined 17% to INR5,952 crores and EBITDA declined 6% to INR636 crores. Consolidated Q4 EBITDA was INR302 crores at a 15.1% margin. Management attributed the weak year to slower industry awarding, project delays, input cost inflation and fixed-cost under-absorption, and it guided to recovery in FY27 led by monetisation cash flows and a 20% revenue growth target.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth target of about 20%, per management.
FY27 order inflow guidance of INR8,000-10,000 crores across roads, railways and power T&D, domestic and international.
FY27 standalone EBITDA margin guided at 9.5-10.5%, described as reaching double digits; management stated FY26 margin was about 8.5%-plus.
Standalone debt expected at INR500-600 crores by March 2027, after about INR1,300 crores of HAM/BOT-linked debt exits.

HAM monetisation: 4 of 6 remaining HAM assets targeted by June 2026 (~INR750+ crores cash); balance 2 by December 2026 (~INR400 crores). Holdbacks of ~INR130 crores expected June-July; deferred toll-extension consideration of ~INR550 crores expected in 24-36 months.
FY27 capex planned at about INR100 crores, including international projects. FY26 capex was INR67 crores, of which Q4 was INR16 crores.
Working capital expected to normalise to 110-120 receivable days by post-September 2026.
Industry: road construction targeted at 9,000-9,500 km in FY27; road capex budgeted at about INR2.9 trillion, up 8%; BOT toll target about INR75,000 crores in FY27.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex INR67 crores total, INR16 crores in Q4 FY26.
FY27 capex planned at about INR100 crores, including international projects.
Tumkur Shivamogga HAM: provisional CODs achieved across multiple stages, improving annuity visibility.
Remaining HAM equity investment about INR325 crores: INR175 crores in FY27, INR75 crores in FY28, INR75 crores in FY29 (Bowaichandi start pending appointed date).
Monetisation of 10 HAM and BOT projects in FY26 (5 HAM and 5 BOT); HAM cash inflow ~INR1,150 crores and BOT ~INR1,800 crores.
demand_pricing: Management says FY26 awarding was slower than expected, with clearance and land delays across the industry.
Q4 input cost pressure from cement, bitumen, steel and fuel, plus labour shortages; budget assumes 0.5%-1% price escalation.
Bid pipeline: about INR40,000 crores of identified NH road projects to bid, plus state opportunities (Bihar, UP) and about INR30,000-40,000 crores of other sectors.

Q4 wins: Diriyah hotel package in Saudi Arabia (INR1,800 crores total, INR900 crores share, executed via SPV); Angola T&D rehabilitation USD72 million (~INR690 crores); Liberia road upgradation USD45 million (~INR430 crores); Bihar Gandak bridge EPC (INR474 crores total, INR242 crores share); IGR Pune LOA; Mumbai traffic management order (via SPV/back-to-back).
Ratings reaffirmed by ACUITE: long-term AA stable, short-term A1+.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Saudi hotel and Mumbai ITMS orders in the standalone order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Saudi Arabia (INR900 crores share) and IGR (INR1,100 crores) are executed by SPVs and sit outside ABL standalone books, captured only in consolidation. Mithi River and traffic management are in the order book under Others, with ABL executing them back-to-back.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 EBITDA margin weak and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited price escalation pressure and year-end ECL provisions of INR28 crores (inventory and debtors). FY27 standalone margin guided at 9.5-10.5%, with ECL reversals expected over time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital situation and what are receivable cycles?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables are milestone-linked. Power T&D cycle is 5-7 months with 30-40% advance; road EPC cycle is about 3-3.5 months. Management expects normalisation to 110-120 days post-September 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why were HAM monetisations delayed and what are the cash inflows?
qa_highlights.answer: Delays are tied to NHAI provisional COD receipts. Completed sales: HAM ~INR1,150 crores and BOT ~INR1,800 crores. Upcoming: ~INR750+ crores from 4 assets by June, ~INR400 crores from 2 by December.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax impact on HAM asset sale gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Capital gains at 12.5%; effective tax about nil at ACL (carry-forward losses) and about INR22 crores at ABL. Combined effective tax on remaining HAM sales estimated at 6-7%.

qa_highlights.question: Are there plans to sell Chennai ORR and Jaora-Nayagaon?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, sale of both is being pursued over the next 12-18 months; a small monetisation process has been launched with good buyer interest.

risks_watch: Standalone revenue down 17% in FY26; FY27 20% growth depends on converting the INR15,312 crore order book and new wins.
ECL provisions (INR28 crores in Q4) and receivable build-up in Power T&D; receivable days must normalise to 110-120 by September 2026.
Monetisation timing depends on NHAI PCOD and appointed dates; INR550 crores deferred toll-extension consideration depends on NHAI decisions.
Input cost inflation (cement, bitumen, steel, fuel) and labour shortages could keep margins under pressure.
NHAI bidder disclosure rule on project casualties and debarment is still being defined by the Road Federation.
Bangladesh order book flat at INR374 crores; management says work continues at slow pace.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term pipeline and monetisation timelines, but cautious on near-term execution and margins, which management attributed to input costs, delays and provisions. Several answers on order-book accounting and HAM timing were specific, while some items (HAM equity invested) were deferred offline.
key_quotes: So execution-wise, next year we should improve by 20%.
So we will definitely reach a 2-digit figure for next year.
We believe that we should go back to the old norms of 110 to 120 days, this is more of a transitory as in the last call also.
So it's a mix of provisions as well as reversions.

adds.what: Remaining HAM equity investment of about INR325 crores (Tumkur Shivamogga stages, Bowaichandi pending appointed date); not new productive capacity

growth.why: FY27 guides about 20% revenue growth and 9.5-10.5% standalone EBITDA margin, backed by a INR15,312 crore order book (plus INR681 crore Angola order) and INR8,000-10,000 crore order inflow target, with HAM monetisation cash flows; no new productive capacity is being added, and Q4 standalone total income fell 10% YoY.
